checkpoints.top_reasoning: Introductions offer occupational personalities but no murder facts. No suspect deserves an evidence-based lead.

But every speaker delivers an equally polished paragraph with a precise grievance plus intimate autobiographical confession. checkpoints.naturalness: Clear sequence and sample contrast create real deduction rather than motive counting. A retained flavoring sample result and bottle custody history are now essential. The unattended period is fairly signaled, although scheduled access needs names and times.

Yet thirty similarly sized confession-and-action speeches again feel like coordinated testimony. Everyone supplies precisely the plot-relevant correction when asked.

Robin and Paige now also demonstrably reached the private glass. Tess succession benefit is conditional and weaker; Artie already refused gift; many corrections independently resolve motives. checkpoints.naturalness: Useful concrete exclusions encourage reconstruction. But the large simultaneous packet supplies an almost mechanical exculpation for many people and repeats closed/open, real/replica, studio/live distinctions at length. The poison treated as a closed preview loan despite unresolved active contents strains ordinary museum safeguards, though the restriction makes institutional negligence coherent.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Justin alone asserts a neutralization correction that the retained clipping expressly does not contain. Active laboratory cyanide and fulfilled original-contents purchase contradict his harmless-remainder account. He visited the unattended glass carrying the historical folder, giving direct opportunity and poison-source knowledge. This is the strongest combined concealment-and-action route, although nobody witnessed him transfer poison. Barb’s blackout and Anya’s cupboard access remain physical alternatives, but their admitted lies have independent documentary explanations.
checkpoints.naturalness: The ending round adds convincing shock and interpersonal repair but nearly every character recites a documentary distinction and accepts a personal fault. Justin’s unusually categorical scientifically false account stands out among neatly resolved confessions, so the solution becomes conspicuous chiefly at the last checkpoint.

final_feedback: I accuse Justin Tyme. His unsupported neutralization story contradicts both the corrected clipping and active-cyanide laboratory findings, while his own visit places him beside the prepared unattended glass. His historical folder gives a plausible knowledge route; reputational exposure and coerced confidentiality provide a motive. The band scrap ties bottle opening to the poisoned glass but has no unique tear match, so it proves the likely method rather than the killer. A lie is not automatically murder: Barb could have used her blackout and room visit, Anya her functioning key and cupboard visit, Chip his band treatment, or Tess/Dada/Minnie/Robin/Paige their glass proximity. Their routes are viable unless timing or transfer evidence rules them out, yet Justin uniquely pushes a false account directly denying the lethal state of the murder source. I am highly confident as a puzzle reader, less confident that this would constitute a uniquely demonstrated prosecution. Suspense holds through stage seven because the clean ingredient, bare glass and accessible bottle narrow method without identifying hands. Stage eight drops a sharp contradictory claim while almost all other deceits receive documented resolutions, making the culprit obvious by editorial pattern. Documentary clues reward reconstructing action rather than counting grievances, but thirty-person mass confession rounds strain conversation and repeat the same confession, correction, personal regret rhythm. Motives cover employment, artistic credit, family power, debt, legitimacy, public benefit and shame; some are resolved before the death and should not be treated as enduring murder incentives. Distinct occupations and relationships help, but voices converge on articulate self-diagnosis. I would prefer fewer polished autobiographical admissions, more interrupted disagreement, and one extra discriminating physical or timing clue against Justin to separate his specific action from mere dishonest interpretation. The institutional failure around an unresolved poison loan is plausible as collective negligence, though many staff casually inspecting it and leaving a poisoned glass unattended feels engineered. The pre-vote story supplies remorse and costs; it leaves whether the actual murderer can be conclusively isolated unresolved.
post_vote_feedback: The reveal confirms Justin Tyme, matching my recorded accusation. His confession efficiently explains preview acquisition, private-glass poisoning, false neutralization and reputational motive. It adds the decisive transfer actions only after the vote; pre-vote clues support a strongest hypothesis but do not independently witness those actions or exclude every physical alternate. This is a fair contradiction puzzle, with a somewhat weaker action-proof puzzle. Justin’s last line about the folder surviving him is a good consequence of his historian identity. The other endings offer concrete costs and relationship choices: Barb surrenders a badge, Anya hands over her spare, Cary faces a repair/job consequence, Anne explains displaced workshop visitors, Sue and Mona choose friendship, and Robin preserves the unresolved claimants’ demand. Those are varied enough to avoid a wholly tidy happy ending. Brie tending crying staff and Al calling home are more immediate and natural than scholarly file recaps. Still, almost every ending uses the same denial, evidence recap, wrongdoing admission, named-person address, forward commitment structure; remorse is distributed with implausible uniform eloquence. Reading all thirty magnifies repetition, while the stated actual-party format of only voted suspects plus murderer would reduce that burden. Artist disputes, wages, ownership, restitution, and personal relationships remain credibly unfinished; these feel like consequences rather than forgotten loose ends. The central unresolved fairness concern is that many nonkiller endings mistake an honest correction or artifact distinction for a murder alibi: a real bottle, bare glass, or recorded petition does not itself prove that person never used poison. No scores or narrative ratings were changed after reveal.
